pieces.title: Canva, Adobe or Claude: who owns design in 2028?
pieces.question: When AI can design a poster in seconds, which design company still gets paid in two years?
pieces.so_what: The design tools your team pays for are turning into agents that work for each other: before renewing Canva or Adobe seats, ask which one your other AI tools can drive.
pieces.hook: Adobe has just opened Photoshop and Premiere so that another company's AI can drive them.
examples: Adobe's new integrations, in preview, let other companies' AI agents drive Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere and After Effects (10 Nov).
Canva and Adobe are both connectors inside Claude Design (Anthropic, June 2026).
Over one million people used Claude Design in its first week (Anthropic, 17 June 2026).
pieces.human: Krish puts the three side by side and scores them on one real job, live, in his own room: the same poster brief given to Canva, Adobe and Claude.

mock.proof: Other companies' AI can now drive Photoshop, Illustrator and Premiere.

pieces.label: Extra piece
pieces.title: ChatGPT now answers with an app. You are a vibe coder and nobody told you.
pieces.question: Will most people who use AI be making their own software within a year, without ever knowing they are doing it?
pieces.so_what: Your staff and customers are about to start making small tools every week without knowing it, because ChatGPT and Claude now answer everyday questions with a working calculator or chart, and almost nobody checks the sums inside.
pieces.hook: Since 8 October, ask ChatGPT what a loan costs and it can hand you a working calculator with sliders, on the free plan.
examples: ChatGPT builds a bill splitter or calculator inside the chat, free users included, from 8 Oct 2026.
Claude's custom visuals are on for every user on web and desktop.
A UC Davis study (7 Nov 2026) found novices checked the data in 3 of 60 sessions.

pieces.title: A 19th-century folk song got a copyright strike from a 500-channel music mill.
pieces.question: How can a song nobody has owned for a hundred years get taken down for copyright?
pieces.so_what: A recording of a song with no known writer was taken off YouTube by a company running about 500 channels, and the appeals failed twice: anyone who records traditional music now knows how the claim system can be turned on them.
pieces.hook: A singer's recording of "Bre Petrunko", a Bulgarian folk song with no known writer, was pulled from YouTube on a claim from Media Nov Records, and her two appeals failed.
examples: About 125,000 views over four years, gone in October.
Media Nov Records runs about 500 YouTube channels.
pieces.human: The song itself plays under the whole explanation, and stops dead at the moment of the takedown.

figure.caption: YouTube channels run by the company that made the claim

pieces.title: TikTok will now watch for fakes of your face. First it needs your ID.
pieces.question: How does an app tell whether a video of you is really you?
pieces.so_what: Creators can now have TikTok watch for videos that use their face without consent, after handing their ID to a third party, and anyone can check whether a clip was made with TikTok's own AI tools: a creator knows what each check can and cannot see.
pieces.hook: TikTok's Likeness Detection flags videos that may use a creator's face, once they verify their ID with a third party; its new AI checker reads hidden labels, and only from its own apps.
examples: ID checks through a third party, Jumio in the US test.
A free checker for TikTok, CapCut, Dreamina, Hypic and Pippit.
Available worldwide to eligible creators from 23 Nov 2026.
pieces.human: Krish runs both checks on a clip of himself, one made in CapCut and one made elsewhere, and reads the answers to camera.

pieces.so_what: A connector lets your chatbot call another app for you, like a guest at the table who does one job. Higgsfield's video tools now plug into ChatGPT and Claude this way: here is what that means and how to add it.

pieces.title: The first AI film in cinemas has a Foley artist.
pieces.question: If a film is sold as made by AI, how many people still made it?
pieces.so_what: The film billed as the first AI-animated feature in cinemas opens on 4 December, and its own director lists the human co-writer, editors, colourists, Foley artist and voice cast behind it: anyone pricing film work can see how much of an "AI film" is still people.
pieces.hook: Gods Don't Give Gifts opens on 4 December as the first AI-animated feature in cinemas, and its director lists the co-writer, editors, colourists, Foley artist and voice actors who made it with him.
examples: Pen drawings at the start of the pipeline.
Four days in a Stockholm studio for the cinema sound mix.
A Foley artist and a voice cast in the credits.

pieces.title: 91% of designers use AI every week. It made them pickier.
pieces.question: If almost every designer now uses AI each week, what is the designer actually doing?
pieces.so_what: Nine in ten designers now use AI every week, up from about half a year ago, while the designers themselves describe careful, methodical work: anyone hiring or briefing a designer knows the gap between "AI does design" and what the job now is.
pieces.hook: In a survey of more than 900 designers, 91% use AI at least weekly, up from 54% a year ago, and the ones who explain it describe more checking, not less.
examples: 91% weekly, up from 54% in a year.
"AI is always my first tool, before I touch code or build a screen."
More than 900 designers surveyed by Designer Fund and Foundation Capital.
